# Project plan

## Start-up phase
<!--
Covering the planning phase, this section should provide a relatively
detailed plan of how work will start on the project. This section is
important because projects need to get up and running quickly.


 - [x] Setting up collaboration platform inc. code for contributors etc.
 - [x] License decisions
 - [x] Reporting framework
-->

ARcenso already has the basic infrastructure in place, allowing the team to begin work on technical deliverables from the first month:

- **Collaboration platform.** The code is hosted in a public [GitHub repository](https://github.com/SoyAndrea/arcenso), with a bilingual (English and Spanish) contributing guide, a code of conduct, continuous integration with `R CMD check`, and test coverage reporting. The package has also undergone a technical review to identify areas for improvement in R package development good practices. During the start-up phase, we will add issue templates for reporting errors in census tables and requesting new tables.

- **License.** ARcenso is released under the MIT license, which will be maintained for all code produced during the project, including the data-processing pipeline.

- **Reporting framework.** The team will hold bi-weekly check-ins to review progress, while project activities and deliverables will be tracked through the public GitHub repository. A short progress report will be prepared every three months, shared with the ISC and made publicly available through the project repository, summarizing completed deliverables, progress in census coverage, and any relevant changes to the project plan.

## Technical delivery
<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->

The project will run for nine months, from January to September 2027, in five phases:

| Phase | Period | Deliverables |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Package infrastructure** | January – March 2027 | Address package quality improvements identified through `pkgcheck`, while maintaining a clean `R CMD check`; restructure internal data storage and data types; and review and adapt existing functions in preparation for CRAN and R-universe distribution. |
| **2. Processing and validation pipeline** | April 2027 | Develop a reproducible data-processing and validation workflow; document the review process; and incorporate the 1991 national-level census tables as the first application of the workflow. |
| **3. Census coverage** | May – August 2027 | Continue the incorporation, standardization, documentation, and validation of the 1960 census and subnational tables from the 1980 and 1991 censuses using the package infrastructure and processing pipeline. |
| **4. Testing, documentation and distribution** | September 2027 | Finalize package testing and technical refinements; update documentation and vignettes; conduct community testing; and prepare ARcenso for distribution through R-universe and submission to CRAN. |


Key target dates:


- **31 March 2027:** Package infrastructure improvements completed, including internal data storage and data types, package quality improvements, and review of existing functions.
- **31 August 2027:** Data-processing and validation pipeline implemented and applied to the planned expansion of census coverage.
- **30 September 2027:** Final project delivery, including package testing, updated documentation and vignettes, community testing, distribution through R-universe, and submission to CRAN.

## Other aspects

<!--
How will you ensure that your work is available to the widest number
of people? Please specify the open-source or creative commons license(s)
you will use, how you will host your code so that others can contribute,
and how you will publicize your work. We encourage you to plan content
to be shared quarterly on the R Consortium blog.

 - [x] Announcement post
 - [x] Delivery blog post
 - [x] Social media
 - [x] UseR!
 - [x] ISC meetings
-->

All code produced through the project will remain openly developed on GitHub under the MIT license, with contributions welcome in both English and Spanish. ARcenso will be prepared for distribution through CRAN and R-universe, and package releases will continue to be archived on Zenodo with a DOI.

To make the project's progress and outputs publicly accessible and support the adoption and dissemination of ARcenso, we plan to:

- **Public project progress.** Maintain a dedicated public section in the ARcenso project documentation to track grant progress, deliverables, and related outputs.

- **R Consortium blog.** Share quarterly updates through the R Consortium blog, documenting ARcenso's technical development, project milestones, and outcomes.

- **Local engagement and communities.** Lead and organize in-person activities in Buenos Aires for R users and others interested in working with census data, together with R en Buenos Aires, RLadies+ Buenos Aires, universities, and other relevant communities and institutions.

- **Conferences.** Submit talks about ARcenso to LatinR and useR! , and other relevant conferences during 2027–2028, sharing the package and the technical experience of developing reproducible infrastructure for historical census data.

- **Social media and R community channels.** Share project progress, releases, and opportunities for use and contribution through social media and relevant R community channels.


## Budget & funding plan

<!--
Note that the maximum grant is $10k USD. The proposal should be in USD.

Outline the milestones for development and how much funding will be
required for each stage (as payments will be tied to project milestone
completion). This also helps the ISC in the event of partial funding. 
Each milestone should specify the work to be done and the
expected outcomes, providing enough detail for the ISC to understand
the scope of the project work and assess the likelihood of success.

We expect that most of the budget will be allocated
for labor costs. We do not cover indirect costs. The ISC grants cannot
cover such things as travel, lodging, food, journal publication fees,
or personal hardware. Cloud services may be covered if they are specific
to the project and the project period. The ISC reserves the right to vet
how funds are used for each project separately. If in doubt, please reach

-->

The requested budget is **USD 5,500** and covers labor only, for a total of **245 hours of team work**, at an effective rate of approximately **USD 22.45 per hour**. The budget is allocated across the four phases described in the Technical delivery section:

| Phase | Period | Team hours | Estimated cost (USD) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| **1. Package infrastructure** | January – March 2027 | 70 | $1,571 |
| **2. Processing and validation pipeline** | April 2027 | 40 | $898 |
| **3. Census coverage** | May – August 2027 | 95 | $2,133 |
| **4. Testing, documentation and distribution** | September 2027 | 40 | $898 |
| **Total** | **January – September 2027** | **245** | **$5,500** |

In the event of partial funding, priority will be given to the package infrastructure and the reproducible processing and validation pipeline, as these provide the technical foundation for the continued expansion of ARcenso beyond the grant period.
